criterion: The header mark at the top left of the home route folds down to the first letter beside the apostrophe on the first scroll.
evaluation_rule: The header mark is the studio name at the top left of every route, the link home. Load the home route, scroll down a little, then scroll back to the very top. Yes if the middle letters of the mark drop out of sight on the first scroll so the first letter sits beside the apostrophe, then return as the visitor reaches the top again. No if the header mark keeps every letter while scrolling, or if the letters vanish in a single frame with the gap left open.

criterion: The home route puts the studio's work and name in front of the visitor, reading as a film the visitor scrolls.
evaluation_rule: The home route is the root address of the studio site, from the white hero down to the closing panel. Scroll the whole route at an easy pace. Yes if the wordmark, the headlines and the imagery fill every window with only small controls at the corners over them, and the scroll moves through the bands without interruption. No if a banner, a pop-up, a persistent navigation bar or any panel covers the work at some point during the scroll.

criterion: The apostrophe of the full wordmark in the home hero arrives after the six letters, growing in place.
evaluation_rule: The hero wordmark is the studio name filling the width of the white first band of the home route. Reload the home route and watch the wordmark as the loading cover lifts. Yes if the six letters appear first and the apostrophe then grows from a point to full size where the apostrophe sits. No if all seven glyphs arrive together, or if the apostrophe slides in from elsewhere.

criterion: The single letters scattered across the home route's object field trail the pointer at different rates like a comet's tail.
evaluation_rule: The object field is the lower stretch of the home route where still objects and single letters float over the black ground. Scroll there on a pointer device, rest the pointer, then sweep the pointer quickly across the window. Yes if the letters chase the pointer, stringing out behind the pointer during the sweep and settling at different moments, the heaviest arriving last. No if the letters stay put, or if every letter moves in lockstep with the pointer.

criterion: The manifesto film band on the home route frames the film with a repeated phrase that corrupts line by line around one clean centre line.
evaluation_rule: The manifesto film band is the full-bleed film near the foot of the home route, after the people band. Read the text at the film's edges and at the film's centre. Yes if the phrase we are naught' repeats in blocks at the edges with characters swapped for lookalikes and the last line of each block turned to noise, while the centre carries We create from nothing. at full strength. No if the edge phrase repeats cleanly with every copy identical, or if the centre line is missing.

criterion: The still objects floating across the home route's object field drift at the objects' own angles, growing as the objects travel with the scroll.
evaluation_rule: The object field is the lower stretch of the home route where a foil star, a chrome heart, a balloon and similar objects float over the black ground. Scroll slowly through that stretch and watch two or three objects. Yes if each object rests at an angle of its own, drifts vertically against the page and grows a little as the object travels. No if the objects scroll rigidly with the page at a fixed size, or if the objects spin on a loop regardless of the scroll.

criterion: The contact row of the menu overlay leads straight into the booking panel on whichever route the visitor is reading.
evaluation_rule: The menu overlay is the full-screen panel opened by the MENU control at the top right; the booking panel is the form that slides in from the right edge to book a call. On the works index, open the menu and choose CONTACT. Yes if the overlay gives way to the booking panel sliding over the works index, with the works index still underneath. No if CONTACT navigates to a separate contact route, or if the overlay stays open over the booking panel.

criterion: Signing in after being turned away from the account page returns the reader to the account page.
evaluation_rule: The account page is where a signed-in reader follows the reader's own enquiries. Signed out, go to the account page, sign in as reader@example.com with the seeded password on the sign-in route that appears. Yes if the reader lands on the account page with the Campaigns enquiry listed. No if the reader lands on the home route or the sign-in route again after a correct sign-in.

criterion: The showreel band on the home route carries a fine grain over the film that strengthens as the film grows to full bleed.
evaluation_rule: The showreel band is the stretch of the home route where the film grows from a framed picture in a rendered room until the film fills the window. Scroll slowly through the band, pausing near the start and again once the film fills the window. Yes if a fine noise texture sits over the film, faint at the start and plainly stronger once the film fills the window. No if the film looks equally clean at both pauses, or if the grain covers other bands of the home route.

criterion: A card on the studio console reads as the works index card on white with a state label and a featured switch added.
evaluation_rule: The studio console is the route an author lands on after signing in, listing every case study as a card. Sign in as author@example.com, look at the Solace card, then compare the Solace card on the works index. Yes if both show the same eyebrow, tagline and cover arrangement, the console card on a white ground adding a Draft or Published label and a featured switch. No if the console shows a table or a list of plain rows, or a card of a different arrangement.

criterion: On the works index, the menu overlay settles gently as the overlay opens, then speeds up as the overlay leaves.
evaluation_rule: The menu overlay is the full-screen panel opened by the MENU control at the top right. Open and close the menu several times, watching the movement. Yes if the opening movement starts fast and slows into place while the closing movement starts slow and speeds away. No if both movements run at one even speed, or if the overlay appears and disappears in a single frame.

criterion: Moving keyboard focus across the service pills of the booking panel shows which pill holds focus at each step.
evaluation_rule: The booking panel is the form that slides in from the right edge after pressing book a call; the service pills are the five outlined choices inside the panel. Open the panel on a case study, press Tab until focus reaches the pills, then move across all five. Yes if at each step one pill carries a visible focus mark that differs from the look of the chosen pill. No if focus moves with no visible mark, or if the focused pill looks identical to the chosen one.

criterion: At a phone width the scattered letters of the not-found route gather toward the middle of the window.
evaluation_rule: The not-found route is the black page served for an unknown address, with large scattered letters and one Homepage pill at the foot. Open an unknown address at a laptop width, then at a phone width, keeping the pointer still. Yes if at the phone width the letters sit closer to the middle of the window than at the laptop width, every letter still on screen. No if letters run off an edge at the phone width, or if the letters keep the laptop arrangement cut down by the narrower window.
